clue.text: Turn round quickly? We will, audibly

indicators.note: audibly asks for a word heard spoken rather than read on the page

parts.note: the contraction of we will, said out loud

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether we will spin about smartly, as if answering a drill order.
explanation.definitionFit: To wheel is to pivot or swing round sharply, as soldiers or birds do.

clue.text: Witty remark made by prudent expert

parts.note: wise means prudent or sensible
crack as an adjective means first-rate or expert, as in a crack shot

explanation.surface: A clever quip from a sensible specialist.
explanation.definitionFit: A wisecrack is a smart, joking comment, so it is a quip or witty remark.

clue.text: Give out beer former husband brought over

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece brought over another is placed above it

parts.note: ex means former
H is the abbreviation for husband
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: Someone hands round beer that an ex-husband carried over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Former husband' reads as one idea, an ex-husband, but the two words are clued separately; 'brought over' places them above the beer in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhale is to breathe out, so it means to give out air or vapour.

clue.text: Vehicle clipped in French district

indicators.note: clipped means trimmed short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a limousine is a large luxury car

explanation.surface: A car was scraped while driving through a region of France.
explanation.definitionFit: The Limousin is a historic region of central France, known for its cattle breed.

clue.text: Fixed food on Sunday

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another is written after it

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for Sunday
tuck is British slang for food, especially sweets and snacks eaten at school

explanation.surface: A menu note says a meal was arranged for Sunday.
explanation.walkthrough: Tuck is British school slang for snacks, as in a tuck shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stuck is held fast in place, unable to move, just as something fixed is.

clue.text: Some hypocrisy, no doubt, in church council

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words, so we look inside them

parts.note: running across the end of the first word, all of the second and start of the third

explanation.surface: A jibe that a church assembly is surely full of double standards.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is an assembly of clergy and sometimes lay members that governs a church.

clue.text: Presumably a social climber must be like a member of the jet set?

definitions.text: Presumably a social climber must be like a member of the jet set?

parts.note: surface: a person trying to rise in society

parts.words: like a member of the jet set
parts.note: setter's reading: the jet set fly about, so they are literally high up and on the move

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase meaning rising socially is read literally as airborne and travelling, which fits jet-setters.
explanation.definitionFit: An upwardly mobile person is one moving up the social ladder, the aim of a social climber.

clue.text: Message seen by locker is of fundamental importance

definitions.note: the answer is a noun used attributively, as in a keynote speech

indicators.note: seen by means placed next to, so the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: a key locks things, so it is a locker
a note is a short message

explanation.surface: A note found by someone's locker turns out to matter greatly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locker' looks like a cupboard; it is anything that locks.
explanation.definitionFit: A keynote sets the central theme, so a keynote address is the main, most important talk.

clue.text: Drinking vessel made of copper found in churned up peat

indicators.note: found in means placed inside something else
churned up means stirred about, so the letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: An archaeologist's find: a copper cup dug out of disturbed peat.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacup is a cup for drinking tea, so it is a vessel for drinking from.

clue.text: Film creature with nuts

parts.note: an animal is a creature
crackers is British slang for mad, like nuts

explanation.surface: A wildlife film about an animal eating nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal Crackers is a 1930 Marx Brothers comedy film.

clue.text: Sea eagles on the Chinese porcelain — method used identifies author

parts.note: the erne is a sea eagle, a crossword favourite
taken as written
Ming is the dynasty whose porcelain is famous
a way of doing something is a method

explanation.surface: A collector's description of eagle motifs on a Ming vase reveals who made it, like an art detective's report.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces join as ERNES + THE + MING + WAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest Hemingway was the American novelist who wrote The Old Man and the Sea.

clue.text: Amusing Colonel drinking mineral

indicators.note: something drinking takes another thing inside itself, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: Col is the usual abbreviation for Colonel
mica is a flaky silicate mineral

explanation.surface: A funny scene: an army colonel sipping mineral water.
explanation.definitionFit: Comical things provoke laughter, which is exactly what amusing things do; the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Subject to work experience

parts.note: under someone's control means subject to it
a machine that works goes

explanation.surface: A phrase from a job advert: applicants are subject to work experience.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo something is to go through or suffer it, which is what to experience means.

clue.text: Unwell, a pair outside with a person providing reliable support

indicators.note: outside says one piece is wrapped around the other rather than placed beside it

parts.note: PR is the abbreviation for pair
ill means unwell
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sick person has a couple of helpers either side of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unwell, a' stays together as the filling; the abbreviation for pair is split to wrap round both.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillar of the community is a figurative term for someone others lean on and trust.

clue.text: Diane's answer is to split up

parts.note: Di is the short form of Diane, so Diane's becomes Di's
to solve a problem is to answer it

explanation.surface: Diane's solution to an unhappy marriage is to separate.
explanation.definitionFit: A partnership or parliament that is dissolved is formally broken up and ended.

clue.text: Type of cheaply made western pasta

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a low-budget cowboy film made in Italy
second meaning: long thin strands of pasta

explanation.walkthrough: Low-budget Italian westerns of the 1960s were nicknamed after the pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the Italian pasta and, as a modifier, a genre of cheap Italian-made cowboy films.

clue.text: Bullfighter to study what's gory in the middle?

parts.note: taken as written
to read a subject at university is to study it

indicators.note: in the middle asks for the central letters of the word, dropping its ends

parts.note: the two central letters of the word

explanation.surface: A bullfighter reads up on the bloodiest part of the spectacle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Read' for study is the British university sense: one reads history.
explanation.definitionFit: A toreador is a bullfighter, especially one on horseback in older usage.

clue.text: Reportedly struggled against misfortunes in US Army post

indicators.note: reportedly points to what is said aloud, so we listen for the sound of the words

parts.note: fought means struggled against; in non-rhotic British speech it sounds the same as the military post
knocks are setbacks or misfortunes

explanation.surface: Soldiers at an American base had a hard time battling bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: The sound match depends on British pronunciation, where the r in the first word is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Fort Knox is a US Army installation in Kentucky, also home to the gold bullion depository.

clue.text: One may be thrown if beer's off

indicators.note: off means gone bad or wrong, so the letters are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: the seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone might get thrown out of the pub if the beer has gone bad.
explanation.definitionFit: A Frisbee is a plastic flying disc made to be tossed between players.

clue.text: Mount beast of burden to cross river

indicators.note: a beast crossing a stream has the water running across its body, so one piece goes through the other

parts.note: the camel is a classic pack animal
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A rider climbs onto a pack animal so as to ford a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' reads as a verb meaning climb on; it is the noun, as in Mount Sinai.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Carmel is a mountain ridge in northern Israel, famous from the story of Elijah.

clue.text: Most recent Los Angeles trial

parts.note: LA is the standard abbreviation for Los Angeles
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: News of the newest court case in Los Angeles.
explanation.definitionFit: Latest is the superlative of late in the sense of recent, so it means newest.

clue.text: Excellent or very bad?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for great or brilliant

explanation.walkthrough: The question plays on slang turning a word for evil into praise, so one word covers both opposites.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang the word is high praise, while its standard sense is morally evil.

clue.text: At home, row about constant prejudice

definitions.note: verb sense: to prejudice someone is to incline them

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the outer words go round the inner one

parts.note: in means at home
c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
a row of things is a line

explanation.surface: A domestic quarrel over a steady bias.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' here works on the two outer pieces at once: they sit either side of the constant like a pair of brackets.
explanation.definitionFit: To prejudice someone is to dispose or lean them towards a view, which is what incline means as a verb.

clue.text: Amongst criminal lawyers everything counted

indicators.note: amongst says the letters lie among the following words

parts.note: running across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A tally of everyone, criminal barristers included.
explanation.definitionFit: In all means in total, with every item added up.

clue.text: People in costume

definitions.note: verb sense: to people a place

parts.note: taken as written
a habit is a costume or outfit, such as a monk's or rider's

explanation.surface: A caption for actors or partygoers dressed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'People' looks like a noun but is the verb, meaning to fill with inhabitants.
explanation.definitionFit: To people an area is to populate it, which is the same as to live in or occupy it.

clue.text: Newly-formed street band likes giving pleasure

indicators.note: something newly formed has been made over, so these letters take a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the fifteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A freshly assembled busking group enjoys bringing joy to passers-by.
explanation.definitionFit: Life is not all beer and skittles is a British idiom: the phrase means fun and easy enjoyment.

clue.text: Very gradually move head of Lenin and stand

parts.note: to ease something is to move it slowly and carefully

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: the opening letter of the name

explanation.surface: Instructions for shifting a statue of Lenin carefully onto a plinth.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a frame that holds up a painting or blackboard, a kind of stand.

clue.text: More than one spoke with one on wireless, endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly says the word loses its final letter
in an across clue, one piece on another is written after it

parts.note: wireless is the old word for a radio set
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone talked at length on the radio, going on without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoke' reads as the past tense of speak; it is the noun, a rod of a wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: The spokes of a wheel run from hub to rim like radii of a circle, so radii is the plural.
